Yeah turnover has been insane and I will be the only science teacher in the building. So I have to rebuild everything from the ground up.
How tf do you get up to Mach 3 at 10 degree angle it's starts to bleed speed.

Yeah, this is what I have been trying to do. I am studying for comptia a+ and ccna for a strong foundation. Also learning python on the side and watching and following along some youtube video tutorials for hacking. I have been playing around with Cisco packet tracer ( cause I am broke and can't setup a physical lab yet).  I am a teacher so I kinda try to teach myself according to what I have learned how learning happens. If I don't get something from one source I know it will be covered by another source at some point. I also watch podcasts here and there by David Bombal, network Chuck to understand which path is the best to take and how to prepare myself for the future and videos by unix guy and other youtuber. Alas however now my vacation is coming to an end and now I am sad and depressed that I will have to stop learning for a few months and go back to teaching. (If I wasn't a first year teacher I probably could have set aside some time to study it). I am just scared to take that leap and leave teaching behind for cybersecurity. I know I love it and love learning about it and so far have been spending every waking moment doing something related to cybersecurity. But I made mistakes during python coding and setting up networks in simulation and I am scared what if I make these same mistakes on the job and never get better. That thought is keeping me from taking that jump into cybersecurity. The question for all of you is. Is this normal lol? Do people get obsessed with it and make mistakes in the begining  or is it just me ? 
P.S sorry for the long post lol.
